subject: gheatmap - how to remove cell border entirely

messages.author: d438361e9afd694e
messages.subject: gheatmap - how to remove cell border entirely
parts:
I'd like to entirely remove the cell border from the phylogenetic heat map because when visualizing 1000's of species, the cells become over-shadowed by the border and less discernible, as shown in this figure:



From the documentation of gheatmap, I see that there is an argument called "color", which changes the color of the cell border. However, I would like to remove it entirely. For example, it would be great if I could simply specify something like: gheatmap(color = "blank")

I've been modifying the code from the vignette to create my figure:

nwk <- system.file("extdata", "sample.nwk", package="treeio")
tree <- read.tree(nwk)
circ <- ggtree(tree, layout = "circular")
df <- data.frame(first=c("a", "b", "a", "c", "d", "d", "a", "b", "e", "e", "f", "c", "f"),
                 second= c("z", "z", "z", "z", "y", "y", "y", "y", "x", "x", "x", "a", "a"))
rownames(df) <- tree$tip.label
df2 <- as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(39), ncol=3))
rownames(df2) <- tree$tip.label
colnames(df2) <- LETTERS[1:3]
p1 <- gheatmap(circ, df, offset=.8, width=.2,
               colnames_angle=95, colnames_offset_y = .25) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option="D", name="discrete\nvalue")
library(ggnewscale)
p2 <- p1 + new_scale_fill()
gheatmap(p2, df2, offset=15, width=.3,
         colnames_angle=90, colnames_offset_y = .25) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="A", name="continuous\nvalue")

My goal is to visualize life-history traits in this huge phylogeny with colors. The gheatmap() function seems like a great way to go, however if there are alternative methods for acquiring a similar effect, I am open to suggestions.

Thanks for this wonderful package!
